documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31 y/o G2P1001, positive home test 6/21. LMP 5/19/22 -> 5w5d, EDD ~2/23/23. Planned. Feels well, a little queasy. No bleeding or pain. On prenatal vitamin with iron daily already.

First pregnancy (2019-20): short cervix found at 22 wks, delivered at term vaginally, healthy daughter.

Vitals as charted. Well. Abd soft NT.
Urine hCG positive.

A/P: Early IUP presumed, 5w5d.
- Continue prenatal vitamin.
- OB referral back to her prior group; mentioned the short cervix history so they can plan cervical length checks.
- Summer break - good timing for early visits.
- Usual precautions.

documents.title: Patient call - anatomy scan
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called, tearful. Had her 18-week anatomy ultrasound at the OB office last Thursday (9/22). Was told the baby has multiple broken bones in the arms and legs and a small chest, and that the baby is measuring small. OB is sending her to the high-risk (MFM) team and following up at her next visit. She has no pain, bleeding or fluid. She wanted us to know and asked to talk to the PCP. Message to PCP.

documents.title: PCP returned call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Robin for about 15 min. She understands the OB and MFM teams will be the ones to explain what the findings mean, and she has a follow-up at 22 weeks. Mostly needed to talk it through. Denies trauma, falls, fevers or illnesses this pregnancy. No fracture history of her own, no bone problems in the family. Husband with her. Offered to see her anytime; she has our number and the after-hours line. Will watch for the OB/MFM notes.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine, pregnant ~20 wks. Screening negative. Influenza quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM L deltoid, VIS given. Tolerated. Pt quiet today; asked how she was doing, she said she is waiting on more appointments and has support at home.

conditions.note: Multiple fetal long-bone fractures, hypoplastic thorax, limb deformities, growth restriction on 18-week anatomy scan; fetal osteogenesis imperfecta suspected

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit, 22 weeks (visit date 10/20/2022)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 10/20/2022
Patient: Robin Parsons, DOB 02/17/1991
G2P1001 at 22w0d by LMP (5/19/22), dated by first-trimester ultrasound.

Reason: Routine 22-week visit and follow-up of the abnormal 18-week anatomy ultrasound.

History: Her first pregnancy was complicated by a short cervix at 22 weeks but went to term with a vaginal delivery of a healthy daughter (2020). This pregnancy was uneventful until the 18-week anatomy survey (9/22/2022), which showed fractures of multiple long bones including both femurs and both humeri, a hypoplastic thorax, limb deformities and fetal growth restriction. She reports no trauma and no infections or febrile illness this pregnancy. She is understandably worried and asks what this means for the baby and why it happened.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron, 1 tab daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: obesity (pre-pregnancy BMI 32). Short cervix in prior pregnancy. PSH: none.
Family history: no known genetic disorders or bone disease in either family.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Vitals stable, within normal limits.
Fundal height appropriate for gestational age. FHT normal by Doppler.

Labs today (maternal): calcium 9.2 mg/dL (8.6-10.2), phosphate 3.5 mg/dL (2.5-4.5), alkaline phosphatase 90 IU/L (30-120 in pregnancy). Maternal bone chemistry normal.

Assessment: IUP at 22w0d with fetal skeletal findings (multiple long-bone fractures, small thorax, limb deformity, FGR) most suggestive of a fetal skeletal dysplasia, likely osteogenesis imperfecta.
Plan: Urgent maternal-fetal medicine consultation with detailed ultrasound and genetics counseling - scheduled 10/25. Discussed in general terms that the findings can carry a serious prognosis and that MFM and genetics will go over this in detail, including testing options. Support resources provided.

cc: Primary care physician

documents.title: Outside OB note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: OB 22-wk note: fetal long-bone fractures, small chest, FGR - suspected fetal OI. Maternal Ca/phos/alk phos normal. MFM consult 10/25. Problem list updated. Will call her after MFM.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation (visit date 10/25/2022)
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
MATERNAL-FETAL MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Regional hospital MFM service
Date of service: 10/25/2022
Referring: outside OB/GYN group. cc: PCP

Dear colleagues,
We saw Ms. Parsons, a 31-year-old G2P1001 at 22w5d, for evaluation of fetal skeletal abnormalities identified at her 18-week anatomy survey.

Detailed ultrasound today: Single live intrauterine pregnancy. Biometry lags dates, consistent with growth restriction. Long bones are short and angulated, with evidence of multiple fractures involving both femurs and both humeri. The thorax is small with a reduced thoracic-to-abdominal circumference ratio, consistent with a hypoplastic thoracic cavity. Limb deformities are present. Cardiac activity present.

Impression: The constellation is most consistent with perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta (type II). Pulmonary hypoplasia from the small chest is the main determinant of prognosis.

Counseling: We met with Ms. Parsons and her husband for an extended visit together with genetic counseling. We reviewed the likely diagnosis, that the expected outcome is not compatible with long-term survival, and the options of continuing the pregnancy with comfort-focused perinatal care or ending the pregnancy by induction of labor. We reviewed that most cases arise from a new (de novo) dominant change in a collagen gene. After discussion she elected amniocentesis for diagnostic confirmation, performed today under ultrasound guidance without complication. Results are expected in about two weeks.

She will let us know her decision regarding the pregnancy; we will coordinate with her OB team and labor and delivery.

Thank you for involving us in her care.
Maternal-Fetal Medicine

documents.title: Labor & delivery discharge summary (admitted 11/01/2022)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - LABOR & DELIVERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 11/01/2022  Discharge: 11/03/2022
Patient: Robin Parsons, 31 y/o G2P1001 -> G2P1101

Admission diagnosis: IUP at 23w5d with fetal skeletal dysplasia, suspected perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta (type II).

Hospital course: After counseling with MFM, genetics and her obstetrician, the patient elected induction of labor. Induction began 11/01/2022. She delivered vaginally on 11/02/2022 at 23w6d; stillbirth. Placenta delivered complete. EBL 250 mL. Postpartum course uncomplicated; afebrile, bleeding appropriate, vitals stable. Bereavement team and chaplain met with the family. Lactation suppression reviewed.

Discharge diagnosis: Delivery at 23w6d following induction for lethal fetal anomaly; stillbirth.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB in 2 weeks; genetics will call with amniocentesis results. Perinatal bereavement support contacts provided.
cc: PCP

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Robin delivered 11/2 at 23w6d after induction; stillborn. Uncomplicated. Problem list updated. Calling her today.

documents.title: PCP call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reached Robin after leaving a message yesterday. Expressed condolences. Physically she is recovering - bleeding light, no fever, no pain beyond mild cramps. Sleeping poorly. Husband is home with her and their daughter. She is on leave from school through the end of the month. Waiting on the genetics call. No thoughts of self-harm. Offered a visit in 2 weeks to check in - she accepted. Front desk to schedule.

documents.title: Genetics results letter (dated 11/14/2022)
documents.author: genetics
documents.body:
MEDICAL GENETICS - RESULTS LETTER
Date: 11/14/2022
Re: Robin Parsons, DOB 02/17/1991 (pregnancy sample)

Dear Ms. Parsons and colleagues,
This letter summarizes our phone discussion of the amniocentesis results from 10/25/2022.

Result: Sequencing of the collagen genes COL1A1 and COL1A2 identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in COL1A1 (a glycine substitution within the triple-helical domain). This result confirms osteogenesis imperfecta and, together with the ultrasound findings, is consistent with the perinatal lethal form (type II).

Interpretation and recurrence: Ms. Parsons has no features of osteogenesis imperfecta herself - no history of fractures, white sclerae and normal hearing by her report - and there is no family history of bone disease. The variant is therefore presumed to have arisen de novo in this pregnancy. Because a small proportion of apparently de novo cases are explained by germline mosaicism in a parent, the recurrence risk in a future pregnancy is low, under 5 percent, but higher than the general population risk.

Recommendations for a future pregnancy: early referral to maternal-fetal medicine, with an early and a detailed anatomy ultrasound focused on the fetal skeleton; diagnostic testing for this familial variant is available if desired.

Please contact us with any questions.
Medical Genetics
cc: OB/GYN; PCP

documents.title: Genetics letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: COL1A1 pathogenic variant, OI type II confirmed in the pregnancy. Presumed de novo; recurrence <5% (possible germline mosaicism). Future pregnancy: early MFM referral. Noted in problem list comment - remember when she next calls with a pregnancy.

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Robin is here 3 weeks after delivering at 23w6d (induction 11/1, stillborn 11/2) for a pregnancy affected by OI type II - COL1A1 variant confirmed on amnio, presumed de novo per genetics.

Physically: bleeding has stopped, no fever, breast engorgement resolved. Saw her OB last week - told recovery is on track.

Emotionally: sad, cries most days, but says she is "functioning" - caring for her daughter, eating, sleeping 6 hours or so. Not anhedonic about everything; enjoys time with her daughter. Going back to her classroom after Thanksgiving and is nervous about questions from colleagues. She and her husband have been to one session with the hospital's bereavement group and plan to keep going. No SI, no thoughts of self-harm. No alcohol.

PHQ-9 5 (sleep, mood, energy).
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron - she asked if she should keep taking it; I said that's fine either way, reasonable to continue if they might try again.
Bivalent COVID booster at pharmacy 10/15 - recorded.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Tearful at times, appropriate, good eye contact. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Grief after second-trimester loss - this is a normal grief response; no depression diagnosis. Continue bereavement group. Reviewed when to reach out sooner (not sleeping, can't get through work, hopeless, any thoughts of self-harm). Offered counseling referral; she'll think about it and message.
2. Hx of pregnancy affected by fetal OI - genetics recommends early MFM in any future pregnancy. Noted.
3. Return-to-work note if the school asks.
4. Follow up in 6-8 weeks or sooner; physical next fall.

documents.body: Hi, HR is asking for a note saying I'm cleared to be back full time (I've been back since Thanksgiving but apparently it never got filed). Sorry for the hassle. Doing a little better, thank you for checking on me.

documents.body: To whom it may concern: Robin Parsons was under my care for a medical leave in November 2022. She was cleared to return to full duty without restrictions as of 11/28/2022. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: RE: Note for school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No hassle at all - letter is attached and in your documents. Glad to hear things are a little better. We never got that follow-up booked; I'll have the front desk offer you a time, and you can always just message.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV (cobas, including types 16 and 18): not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical with Pap/HPV
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

32 y/o, here for physical. Last seen 11/2022 after her loss; the planned follow-up never got scheduled. She says the spring was hard but things feel steadier now - kept going to the bereavement group through June, back to herself at school. Daughter started preschool. They have not decided about another pregnancy; if they do, she knows to message early so we can get her to MFM. Still taking prenatal vitamin most days.

No new symptoms. Weight about the same as last year. Swimming at the town pool this summer, 2-3x/wk.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA.
SH: married, teacher, never smoker, no EtOH.
PHQ-2 0.
Pap overdue (last 2018).

Exam: BMI 33. Well appearing, bright affect. HEENT nl. Neck no LAD or thyromegaly. CV RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft NT. Pelvic: normal external genitalia and vagina, parous cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected; bimanual normal. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: Pap with HPV co-test today. CBC, lipids, A1c. Flu shot today; updated COVID vaccine when available at the pharmacy.
2. Obesity class I (BMI 33): stable. She likes swimming; encouraged keeping something going through winter. Revisit in 6 months - she agreed to a spring check.
3. Hx pregnancy affected by fetal OI (COL1A1, presumed de novo): early MFM referral with any pregnancy.
4. Mood: much improved, screen negative today.
RTC 6 months (weight), 1 yr physical.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin - Pap normal and HPV negative, so the next one is in 5 years. Blood counts and cholesterol fine, A1c normal. Front desk will set up the spring check-in.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 33F.

Interval: well, no illnesses. Skipped the spring check (conferences). Weight unchanged from last year. Kept swimming until October last year then stopped; walks at lunch with another teacher now.

They are thinking about trying again next year. Reviewed plan: message as soon as she has a positive test, we confirm and send her to OB and MFM together for early and detailed scans per genetics. Continue prenatal vitamin with iron.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA.
PHQ-2 0. Mood good.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BMI 33. Well. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. CV regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin no acanthosis.

A/P
1. Obesity class I (BMI 33) - pre-pregnancy counseling: even modest loss before conception lowers GDM risk; she has her grandmother's diabetes in mind. Offered nutrition referral again - declined, wants to try a meal-planning approach with her husband.
2. Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c.
3. Flu shot today. Updated COVID at pharmacy.
4. Pap/HPV next 2028.
RTC 1 yr or with a positive pregnancy test.
